actor.active.text: If false, the actor is skipped: no update, no collision, OAM slot released.

actor.priority.text:
Drawing order against the BG layers.
0 = in front of every background, 3 = behind them all.
GBA: OAM attribute 2, bits 10–11.

actor.screen_space.text:
Anchors the actor to the SCREEN instead of the world: it no longer scrolls with the camera. This is UI made of sprites — score, hearts, cursor — with the whole usual SpriteComponent (states, animations, sprite editor).

X and Y become SCREEN pixels (0–239, 0–159), the same frame of reference as screen-anchored interface elements.

GBA: OAM attribute 0, bits 10–11.

actor.x.text:
Horizontal position in pixels (0–239).
Read: local px = self.position.x
Write: self.position = vec2(x, y), or self:move(self.position, speed)

actor.y.text:
Vertical position in pixels (0–159).
Read: local py = self.position.y
Write: self.position = vec2(x, y), or self:move(self.position, speed)

camera.mode.text:
Fixed: stays where activation put it.
Follow: keeps the chosen Actor inside a deadzone.
Script: the engine computes nothing, the script decides.

camera.position.text: Reflects dragging the yellow rectangle in the canvas — editing here moves it too. Applied every time the camera is activated (scene start, or camera.switch).

camera.frame.text: Screen size the camera renders into (max 240×160). Smaller than full screen → the camera claims one of the scene's two windows while active (which one is decided at build — cf. Windows panel, Scene inspector).

camera.margin.text: Deadzone: the camera only moves once the Actor gets further than Margin X/Y from the screen edge.

camera.bounds.text: Applied when the camera is activated. A script can redefine them afterwards with camera.bound = rect(x, y, w, h).

camera.script.text: Runs AFTER the declarative settings above and BEFORE world bounds are applied — so it adjusts the framing instead of fighting it.

collision.solid.text:
true → stopped by the collision map.
false → trigger: the map ignores it.
The on_collision_* handlers fire either way.

collision.tag.text: Collision group, shared between actors. The matrix in Project Settings ▸ Collisions decides which groups ignore each other; codegen emits it as BOXTAG_<TAG>. Pick an existing tag from the list, or type a new one.

collisions.empty.text: Declare at least two tags for the matrix to mean something — with the button below, or by tagging an actor's Collision component.

collisions.symmetry.text:
Only the checked pairs are tested, and a collision is always symmetric: if A hits B, then B hits A.
An unchecked pair is not emitted at all — no code, and no test per frame.

collisions.usage.text: Uncheck a pair so those two tags ignore each other. Drag a handle to reorder.

data.column_rename.text: Renaming a column is done in the grid header — it is written as code in scripts, so the rename rewrites them.

settings.tips.text: Tips are the explanations: what a concept means, where an optimisation is worth it. Warnings about what the build or the screen will do are never hidden by this.

ui.anchor.forced_actor.text: Target forced — anchored on an actor: an actor moves by the pixel, the BG grid advances by 8.

ui.anchor.forced_bitmap.text: Target forced — scene in mode {mode} (bitmap): there is no tilemap.

ui.anchor.no_actor.text: Anchored on an actor, but no actor chosen: the interface will land at the screen origin.

ui.fill.bg.text: Tiled background, cropped on bottom/right if the zone is smaller. BG target only.

ui.fill.color.text: A palette entry (index 0 = transparent on hardware). Texts inside the container compose on it instead of punching through it; a text's own Highlight overrides it.

ui.fill.color_inactive.text: “{palette}” is not among the scene's active BG palettes: the build drops this background. Add it in the scene inspector, or pick one of the active palettes.

ui.fill.nine.text: Stretchable frame: fixed corners, repeated edges/center. Margins belong to the UI background — editing them here changes every container using it.

ui.fill.sprite.text: Sprite tiled across the container — the only background that exists on OBJ target, where there is no tilemap.

ui.fill.sprite_cost.one: {w}×{h} tiled {cols}×{rows} = {n} OAM slot of the 128 the hardware has, actors included. Tiles cost nothing extra: every cell points at the same frame.
ui.fill.sprite_cost.other: {w}×{h} tiled {cols}×{rows} = {n} OAM slots of the 128 the hardware has, actors included. Tiles cost nothing extra: every cell points at the same frame.

ui.fill.sprite_overflow.text: The last column/row overflows by {dx}×{dy} px: the hardware cannot crop a sprite.

ui.image.cost.one: {w}×{h} px  ·  {n} frame across all states  ·  {where}. Every state stays resident: a script may switch at any frame.
ui.image.cost.other: {w}×{h} px  ·  {n} frames across all states  ·  {where}. Every state stays resident: a script may switch at any frame.

ui.image.missing.text: Sprite “{sprite}” not found in the project.

ui.image.none.text: No sprite bound — nothing will be drawn here.

ui.image.where_obj.one: 1 OAM slot, sharing the sprite's {n} tile already in OBJ VRAM
ui.image.where_obj.other: 1 OAM slot, sharing the sprite's {n} tiles already in OBJ VRAM

ui.layout.shared.one: Shared by {n} scene — editing it changes that scene too.
ui.layout.shared.other: Shared by {n} scenes — editing it changes them all.

ui.list.cursor_missing.text: Cursor "{name}" is not an image of this layout — the list will navigate without one.

ui.list.empty.text: No rows: place text zones INSIDE this list. Those are what it walks.

ui.list.rows.one: {n} row: {names}. The script writes their content — menu:row(n) gives the zone.
ui.list.rows.other: {n} rows: {names}. The script writes their content — menu:row(n) gives the zone.

ui.text.anim_bg.one: {n} animated glyph in this text, but a background zone cannot animate it — it will render static. Anchor the zone on an actor to get sprites.
ui.text.anim_bg.other: {n} animated glyphs in this text, but a background zone cannot animate them — they will render static. Anchor the zone on an actor to get sprites.

ui.text.anim_capped.one: {n} animated glyph reserved — capped at {max}, the rest renders static.
ui.text.anim_capped.other: {n} animated glyphs reserved — capped at {max}, the rest renders static.

ui.text.anim_reserved.one: {n} animated glyph reserved (from the text itself).
ui.text.anim_reserved.other: {n} animated glyphs reserved (from the text itself).

ui.text.bank_none.text: No slot chosen above: text can't read any color yet, and the pickers below only show numbers. Font ink (index 0) still works — it's the font's own color.

ui.text.bank_inherited.text: Bank inherited from '{container}' — a text inside a filled container reads its ink there, not the scene bank. To change it, change the container's fill.

ui.priority.bg.text: Priority applies when this element renders as a sprite (its node follows an actor). Here it sits on a BG layer, so its depth is the layer's.

ui.text.key_none.text: No entry yet — typing here creates one.

ui.text.key_shared.one: Shown by {n} other element — fixing the entry fixes both, breaking it breaks both.
ui.text.key_shared.other: Shown by {n} other elements — fixing the entry fixes them all, breaking it breaks them all.

ui.text.sample_only.text: No entry: a script writes here. The sample is editor-only — it sizes the box and feeds the canvas, and is never compiled.

ui.visible.hidden_parent.text: Hidden anyway — parent “{parent}” is not visible.
